sections.h2: Shaded decks and sunny decks age differently
body: A deck behind a riverfront house in Three Rivers Estates or near Ichetucknee may spend most of the day in shade. It stays damp, grows algae that makes the boards slick, and softens first where leaves pile up. A deck on open ranch land has the opposite problem: UV grays the surface, the boards check and split, and the stain wears off the walking paths. Deck staining in Fort White, FL handles both, but the cleaning, drying time, and stain choice are different for each.

Peeling usually means a film-forming product was applied too thick, or over wood that was still wet. Water gets behind it and lifts it. The fix is to strip the failing coating, clean the wood, let it dry, and switch to a penetrating stain that soaks into the fibers. Our Florida deck and fence staining guide goes into the product differences.

bullets: Probe boards, treads, and posts for rot
Replace damaged boards and reset fasteners
Strip failed coatings and treat mildew
Dry, then sand raised grain and gray fibers
Spray, then back-brush stain into the grain
body: Back-brushing pushes stain into board gaps and end grain, where water gets in first. Rot found during the walkthrough is listed and priced before we start. Our article on deck wood rot signs shows what we probe for.

Semi-transparent stain is a good choice for most Fort White decks, showing grain while blocking more UV than a clear finish. Solid stains suit older decks with mismatched boards. Shaded decks need extra drying time after washing, so the schedule allows for that, and we check the boards again before the first coat. Stair treads and the boards near doors wear fastest, so we look at those closely and may recommend a maintenance coat on just those areas between full restains. The best season is October through May, and summer work starts early in the day.
If a fence or railing runs off the deck, the Fort White fence painting crew can match the color. For the wider service, see deck and fence staining. For local background, see the Fort White overview.

faqs.q: Can you stain a deck that is always in the shade?
faqs.a: Yes, but it needs a thorough mildew treatment and more drying time before staining. We check that the wood is dry before applying anything.

faqs.q: Why did my last deck stain peel?
faqs.a: Usually a film-forming product went on too heavy or over damp wood. We strip it and switch to a penetrating stain.

faqs.q: Do you repair boards before staining?
faqs.a: Yes. Damaged boards, treads, and fasteners are listed on the estimate and fixed before any stain goes on.
Solid stains generally last longer than transparent ones, but they hide the grain. Semi-transparent is a common middle ground.
